retained_skill: Recovering every checksum-valid record from a structurally damaged binary log while interpreting each record in its device byte order.
bottleneck: Ten attempts omitted the seven big-endian records and recovered only 28 records; the two attempts that did recover all 35 were nevertheless rejected because the verifier required decimal-rounded values rather than the native IEEE-754 numbers requested by the instruction.
change: Repair in the scratch verifier: compare each recovered numeric value to the documented record value with a small floating-point tolerance instead of requiring exact equality with a two-decimal literal. This is grader-side help at the original correctness signal; it removes the hidden representation obstacle while leaving mixed-endian discovery and recovery entirely with the student.
restore: No later restoration is appropriate: exact two-decimal serialization was never a public requirement, so the semantic numeric comparison is a permanent verifier repair rather than removable task help.
prediction: The change addresses the final exact-value comparison that rejects attempts 03 and 11 after they recover all 35 records. Their unchanged next action—submitting native unpacked float values—will now satisfy the numeric content check; this is refuted if either replay still fails any retained check after the repair.
